attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The derivation is finite-dimensional and valid once B and N are supplied, but Yang-Mills analysis has not yet proved that the reflected Wilson boundary OPE yields trivial quotient holonomy or a PSD real modulus quotient on the realized locked Wilson cone.
steps: Start from regulated reflection positivity: for every finite collar family, Q_{a,L}(T_\delta F,c)\ge0. RG convergence of fixed-collar reflected probes gives N^\delta\to N entrywise, hence N\succeq0 by closedness of the finite PSD cone.

The target OS form is not N if collar collapse contributes a boundary factor. Under the multiplicative boundary OPE N=B\circ M, the same-theory target is M=B^{[-1]}\circ N. Therefore the closed-cone lemma proves positivity of N, but the missing bridge is positivity of this Schur preimage M.

Normalize to positive diagonal and write M_{ij}=r_{ij}e^{i\theta_{ij}}. A diagonal unitary U changes phases by \theta_{ij}\mapsto\theta_{ij}+u_j-u_i, so phases are removable exactly when their cycle sums vanish. On triples this invariant is \Phi_{ijk}=\theta_{ij}+\theta_{jk}-\theta_{ik}.

After quotient phases are removed, the test reduces to the real symmetric matrix R with R_{ii}=M_{ii} and R_{ij}=|M_{ij}|. PSD of R is still substantive; pairwise bounds only give 2 by 2 minors. The first non-pairwise obstruction is the 3 by 3 determinant formula above.

Thus the proof route is: prove boundary quotient holonomy vanishes for reflected Wilson triples, then prove the real modulus quotient is PSD on every realized finite Wilson family. Conversely, any negative principal minor of B^{[-1]}\circ N is a falsifier even though the collar-limit matrix N remains positive.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: It reduces OS positivity to explicit boundary OPE invariants, but it does not compute or bound those invariants for continuum Yang-Mills Wilson hairpins. The hard estimate remains analytic: control coincident reflection-plane Wilson products without changing the theory.

assumptions: Fixed-collar RG convergence is strong enough to pass every reflected Wilson OS matrix entry to a limit N_{ij}.

The boundary collision of reflected Wilson collars admits a multiplicative leading factor B_{ij} with no zero entries on the finite support being tested, after diagonal one-body renormalizations already included in the locked observable definition.
Additive positive contact terms have zero diagonal after diagonal trace continuity and hence vanish by Cauchy-Schwarz; any surviving additive term is treated as a separate falsifier.
The realized Wilson cone is not assumed to be all PSD matrices; all positivity tests are only claimed for matrices actually produced by locked Wilson observables.
definitions: source object: finite families of regulated gauge-invariant Wilson collar observables T_\delta F_i whose fixed-collar Schwinger matrices N^\delta_{ij}=S(\Theta T_\delta F_i,T_\delta F_j) have OS-positive limits N.

target object: the intended continuum OS matrix M_{ij}=S(\Theta F_i,F_j) on the locked gauge-invariant Wilson test algebra, before adding boundary counterterms or changing loop renormalization at the reflection plane.

controlled interface: a boundary OPE factorization N=B\circ M with nonzero Hermitian boundary factor B, together with the Schur-preimage test M=B^{[-1]}\circ N on each finite realized Wilson support graph.

same-theory condition: B must be a removable collar artifact for the same locked observables; if removing B requires enlarging the algebra, changing Wilson-loop normalization at t=0, or adding a boundary Hilbert sector, the bridge is not a proof for the original Yang-Mills theory.

equations.valid_when: The 3 by 3 target matrix is normalized by positive diagonal entries and r_{ij}=|M_{ij}|/\sqrt{M_{ii}M_{jj}}=|N_{ij}/B_{ij}|/\sqrt{M_{ii}M_{jj}}.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find three realized reflected Wilson hairpins with pairwise valid inequalities r_{ij}\le1 but 1+2r_{12}r_{23}r_{13}\cos\Phi_{123}-r_{12}^2-r_{23}^2-r_{13}^2<0; this is a decisive triangle falsifier for same-theory OS positivity.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Turns the previous finite Schur-preimage slogan into a computable bridge: phase holonomy handles the unitary part, while PSD of the real modulus quotient handles the remaining OS positivity.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Finite Wilson OS positivity after collar removal is valid if the boundary OPE quotient matrix has trivial phase holonomy and positive real modulus quotient on every realized locked Wilson family. More precisely, let N be the positive collar-limit OS matrix and suppose the same-theory boundary factorization N_{ij}=B_{ij}M_{ij} holds with B_{ij}\ne0. The intended OS matrix M is positive exactly when B^{[-1]}\circ N is positive; this can be tested by first removing quotient phases when their cycle holonomy vanishes, then checking PSD of the remaining real modulus quotient. A nonzero triangle holonomy or a negative real quotient minor is a concrete falsifier of the same-theory bridge.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if the reflected Wilson boundary OPE necessarily introduces nontrivial boundary Hilbert data or if the locked Wilson algebra cannot realize enough finite matrices to test the quotient invariants.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if one proves, on a dense locked Wilson core, that all quotient phase holonomies vanish and all real modulus quotient matrices are PSD, with fixed-collar RG convergence already supplying N\succeq0.
control_decision.reason: The branch continues to produce sharper, falsifiable bridge obligations rather than repeating the closed-cone topology. The next step is concrete and finite: calculate or bound quotient holonomy and modulus determinants for reflected Wilson hairpin triples.

falsifiers: A three-hairpin Wilson calculation with nonzero quotient phase holonomy and negative normalized determinant, even though every pairwise damping inequality is valid.
A boundary OPE factor B with zeros on a realized Wilson support edge, making the Schur preimage ill-defined without changing the observable algebra.
A surviving additive boundary contact with zero diagonal but nonzero off-diagonal, contradicting positive-contact Cauchy-Schwarz and exposing an invalid boundary decomposition.
A modulus quotient R_{ij}=|N_{ij}/B_{ij}| that passes all 2 by 2 tests but has a negative 4 by 4 or larger principal minor on realized Wilson observables.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 204 sharpened the post-collar obstruction into a two-layer finite invariant test. The closed-cone argument is valid for collar-limit matrices N, but same-theory OS positivity is exactly the positivity of M=B^{[-1]}\circ N. This is not decided by B alone and not by pairwise damping alone. The first genuinely new falsifier is a triangle determinant controlled by quotient phase holonomy; after phases are coboundaries, the remaining modulus quotient must still be PSD on realized Wilson families. The next Yang-Mills work is therefore a boundary OPE computation for reflected Wilson triples and then higher principal minors.
